version.changelog: 新增能力路由与异步任务闭环，修复失效引用、Token 泄漏和 Skill 元数据兼容性

llm.summary: The skill appears to do what it says: submit Facebook profile URL collection jobs to Dataify using a Dataify API token, with some privacy and token-use considerations to understand first.

dimensions.detail: The helper reads DATAIFY_API_TOKEN from the environment and sends profile URLs plus the token-authenticated request to Dataify, which is expected for this integration but should be clear to users.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains markdown instructions, agent metadata, static SVG assets, and one Python helper script; no hidden install hook or automatic persistence mechanism was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Invocation wording is broad and implicit invocation is enabled, but the workflow requires parameter confirmation before submission and stays within the Dataify/Facebook-profile task scope.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill recommends a long-term DATAIFY_API_TOKEN environment variable but says to ask before saving and only gives user-run commands; it does not silently write credentials.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose, instructions, and script all align around submitting Dataify Builder jobs for Facebook profile URLs and returning task status.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to use Dataify to collect Facebook profile data by URL. Before running it, make sure you are allowed to collect the profiles you submit, understand that the profile URLs are sent to Dataify, and treat DATAIFY_API_TOKEN as a credential that authorizes actions on your Dataify account.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Outbound submission to Dataify and use of a Dataify token are core to the skill; the artifact could disclose the third-party transfer more plainly, but the endpoint, Authorization header, and Dataify workflow are visible.
[SQP-1] expected: The trigger text is broader than ideal and implicit invocation is enabled, but it remains centered on this Dataify Facebook profile collection workflow and includes confirmation before submission.
[SQP-2] expected: Facebook profile URLs and authenticated requests are sent to Dataify as part of the declared task; the missing plain-language privacy warning is a user-awareness issue, not evidence of hidden behavior.
[EA2] expected: Using an existing DATAIFY_API_TOKEN without re-entering it is conventional API-client behavior, and the skill does not silently persist new tokens; users should still understand that a saved token may be used for submissions.
